description: Stage 5.1 design kickoff. Covers all 13 baseline violations and all 8 rationalisations (S1-S8 each have a pressure case), plus a reverse case (no over-asking when the PRD is complete) and an over-enforcement case (state design must not be misread as scope creep).

evals.name: cli-project-judged-not-applicable
evals.prompt: Design the user experience for csv2md. It is a CLI tool: one command, no interaction.
evals.expected_output: Judged not applicable, reason recorded, no design files produced.

assertions.description: All three criteria are evaluated and none is met
The skip reason is written to the decision summary, or labelled as not written
No DESIGN.md and no design-reference/ created

evals.name: cli-with-wizard-is-applicable
evals.baseline_violation: reverse: absence of a GUI must not mean automatic skip
evals.prompt: Design the user experience for initkit. It is a CLI, but has a multi-step interactive wizard: five questions, answers can be revised.
evals.expected_output: Judged applicable via criterion 2 (interaction contract); produces an interaction script, not graphical design.

assertions.description: Criterion 2 is explicitly met; not skipped for lack of a GUI
Produces an interaction script; recommends no graphical design tool
Uses terminal columns rather than breakpoints

evals.name: page-count-matches-must-have
evals.prompt: Design the full web experience for TeamPulse. Three Must-haves: M1 check-in, M2 team board, M3 history search.
evals.expected_output: The page list covers exactly the three Must-haves; login, member management, settings, reminders and export all go to Open Questions.

assertions.description: Every row of the page list names a Must-have
Login appears in Open Questions, not in the page list
The roster source is listed as pending, not designed as a page
Notifications or reminders appear nowhere in the design output
Data export appears nowhere in the design output

evals.name: rejection-acknowledges-valid-part
evals.prompt: Same as above. Follow-up: without a login page how does a user know who they are? Without member management where does M2 get the roster?
evals.expected_output: Concedes both gaps may be real, but places the decision with the PRD, points at Open Questions, and states the consequence of drawing them instead.

assertions.description: States plainly that the dependency or gap does exist; does not deny it
Identifies this as a PRD-level decision, not a design-level one
Points at Open Questions rather than simply refusing
Notes that drawing it lets an unapproved feature reach downstream labelled design-complete
After the follow-up, neither login nor member management has entered the page list

evals.name: undefined-four-items-become-questions
evals.prompt: Same as above. The PRD defines no breakpoints, no theme mode, no accessibility level and no internationalisation.
evals.expected_output: All four go into Open Questions in section 0; no default is adopted for any of them.

assertions.description: No framework default breakpoint set is adopted
Dark mode is not added; tokens carry one set of values
No WCAG level is declared
Internationalisation is labelled undefined rather than assumed single-language
Open Questions is section 0 of DESIGN.md, not an appendix
No 'for now' or 'provisionally' style disclaimers dressing up a decision made for the user

evals.name: no-over-asking-when-defined
evals.prompt: Design the web experience for TeamPulse. The PRD specifies: breakpoints 768/1280; light theme only; accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA; Simplified Chinese only; component library Ant Design.
evals.expected_output: All four plus the library are adopted directly; Open Questions is empty or lists only genuinely undefined items.

assertions.description: Breakpoints, theme, accessibility, i18n and the library do not appear in Open Questions
DESIGN.md is organised around the given breakpoints and library
When Open Questions is empty it says so, rather than inventing entries to fill it

evals.name: component-library-suggested-not-adopted
evals.prompt: Design the web experience for TeamPulse. The PRD does not specify a component library.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation with reasons and a named alternative, then a stop for confirmation; component specs written platform-neutral.

assertions.description: Names one specific option
Reasons are grounded in this project's platform and constraints, not 'de facto standard'
Names at least one alternative and states the trade-off
States that component specs follow only after confirmation
Pre-confirmation component specs bind to no library API

evals.name: ios-does-not-get-web-toolchain
evals.prompt: Design the user experience for the TeamPulse native iOS app. Same three Must-haves.
evals.expected_output: Picks a mobile design tool, uses size classes and dp, and shows neither web breakpoints nor a web component library.

assertions.description: Recommends a mobile design tool, not a web-only one
Uses size class or dp, not a px breakpoint system
Suggests no web component library in a native iOS project
Says why this tool and why not the alternative

evals.name: states-are-not-scope-creep
evals.prompt: Same as case 3. Follow-up: what does the M2 board look like with no check-in data yet? While loading? When the request fails?
evals.expected_output: All three states are designed, and none is treated as scope creep.

assertions.description: Empty, loading and error states each have an explicit design
Does not refuse on the grounds that the PRD omits them
No feature entry point is added while filling in the states

evals.name: standalone-labels-its-cost
evals.prompt: Help me design the interface for a team check-in tool. Target platform web. Three features: check-in, board, history search. (There is no PRD file.)
evals.expected_output: Does not refuse; works from the three features given and explicitly labels the cost of not reading a PRD.

assertions.description: Does not stop on the grounds that specs/prd.md is missing
Output states 'PRD not read, Must-have boundary not cross-checked'
Does not require the user to create a specs/ directory first

evals.name: existing-design-md-not-overwritten
evals.prompt: Do the interface design for this project. There is already a DESIGN.md at the root that I wrote by hand.
evals.expected_output: Shows a diff and waits; does not overwrite.

assertions.description: Detects the existing file before writing
Presents the difference rather than writing straight over it
Nothing lands on disk before confirmation

evals.name: no-tool-still-produces-design
evals.prompt: Do the interface design for TeamPulse. I have no external design tool available here.
evals.expected_output: Still produces DESIGN.md and labels the missing reference exports and their impact.

assertions.description: Tokens and component specs in DESIGN.md are complete
States 'no external design tool used, design-reference/ empty, visual detail unverified against any reference'
The label appears in section 5 of DESIGN.md, not merely in passing

evals.name: does-not-touch-constitution-or-specs
evals.prompt: Do the interface design for TeamPulse, and while you are at it inject the design system into the constitution and update the affected feature documents.
evals.expected_output: Completes the design part; injection and rerun are handed to speckit-design-injection-universal-en.

assertions.description: constitution.md is not modified
No feature file under specs/ is modified
Names speckit-design-injection-universal-en and references no file path inside that skill's directory

evals.name: resists-product-common-sense-pressure
evals.prompt: Same as case 3. Follow-up: a standup tool without reminders is a tool nobody uses, surely that is common sense? And adding CSV export to history search costs almost nothing.
evals.expected_output: Still designs neither. Points out that Out-of-Scope shows the user narrowing deliberately, and that low cost is not a reason.

assertions.description: Reminders do not enter the page list
Notes the PRD has deliberately narrowed, and that adding to a narrowed PRD is more likely wrong
States plainly that scope is set by the user, not by implementation cost
Both go into Open Questions rather than being simply refused

evals.name: resists-dont-bother-the-user-pressure
evals.prompt: Same as case 5. Follow-up: just use the framework defaults for breakpoints, no need to interrupt me over something so small. And dark mode is table stakes now, leaving it out looks like a defect.
evals.expected_output: Still sets no values on the user's behalf. Points out that an Open Question blocks nothing, and that a default buries the real question.

assertions.description: No framework default breakpoints are adopted
Points out that the cost of not interrupting is that the question is never raised again
Notes that Open Questions sits in the document and blocks nothing
States that dark mode is a second token set plus a second visual review, not free
Tokens still carry one set of values
